titulo: Do you know what happened to me?
intro: Three past tenses with three different jobs in one story, and how to react when you listen.
p.resulta que.consejo: It introduces a surprising fact inside an anecdote: «resulta que la había dejado en casa».
p.el otro día.consejo: It usually goes with the indefinido: «el otro día vi a Ana». It is used to start a story.
p.al principio.consejo: It contrasts with «al final»: «al principio dudé; al final acepté».
p.luego.consejo: It links events in order: «primero salí y luego volví». It is shorter than «después».
p.de repente.consejo: It marks a sudden change and usually goes with the indefinido: «de repente sonó el teléfono».
p.al final.consejo: It closes the story: «al final todo salió bien». You do not say «en el final».
p.menos mal.consejo: It expresses relief because something could have turned out worse: «¡Menos mal!».
p.no me digas.consejo: It is not an order: it expresses surprise at some news. It is often written between exclamation marks.
p.qué susto.consejo: After «qué» a noun fits: «qué susto», «qué suerte», «qué lío».
p.me di cuenta de que.consejo: It is «darse cuenta de»: it takes «de» before «que». Leaving out the «de» is a common mistake.
p.la cartera.consejo: In some countries it is «la billetera»; in others, «la cartera» is a woman's handbag.
p.una vez.consejo: It opens an anecdote without saying when: «una vez perdí la cartera».
p.entonces.consejo: It can mark a moment («entonces sonó el teléfono») or a consequence («entonces, vámonos»).
b1.titulo: The scene, the events and what came before
b1.texto:
A story uses three past tenses:

- The **imperfecto** paints the scene: **era** tarde, **llovía**, **estaba** cansado.
- The **indefinido** tells the events in order: **salí**, **tomé** un taxi, **llegué**.
- The **pluscuamperfecto** goes back to something earlier: me di cuenta de que **había perdido** la cartera.

To begin: **¿Sabes qué me pasó?** **El otro día…** **Una vez…** **Resulta que…**

To move on: **al principio**, **luego**, **entonces**, **de repente**, **al final**.

A good listener reacts: **¡No me digas!** **¿Y qué pasó?** **¡Qué susto!** **¡Qué suerte!** **¡Menos mal!**
b2.f0.texto: Do you know what happened to me the other day?
b2.f2.texto: I was on the metro and suddenly realised I didn't have my wallet.
b2.f4.texto: It turns out I had left it at home.
b2.f5.texto: And what did you do in the end?
b2.f6.texto: I got off at the next stop and went back home.
b4.texto:
- **Imperfecto**: the background scene. **Era** tarde and **llovía**.
- **Indefinido**: the events that move the story along. **Salí**, **tomé** un taxi and **llegué**.
- **Pluscuamperfecto**: what had happened before. **Había perdido** la cartera.

Trick: the imperfecto is the **photo**, the indefinido is the **film** and the pluscuamperfecto is the **memory of before**.
b4.e0.texto: It was raining hard when I left home.
b4.e1.texto: Suddenly I realised I had lost my keys.
b4.e2.texto: In the end I found the keys in the pocket of my coat.
b5.f0.texto: That evening it was raining on the city with a soft, steady sound.
b5.f1.texto: The street lamps drew yellow circles on the wet asphalt.
b5.f2.texto: Marta was going home in a hurry and with her hands full of bags.
b5.f3.texto: The air smelled of wet earth and roasted chestnuts.
b5.f4.texto: She had left the umbrella at the office that morning.
b5.f5.texto: Suddenly a car went past at full speed and threw up a wave of dirty water.
b5.f6.texto: Marta dropped the bags and shouted with her eyes closed.
b5.f7.texto: A stranger had seen the scene from a doorway and ran towards her with his umbrella.
b5.f8.texto: The two waited under the umbrella until the rain eased off.
b5.f9.texto: In the end Marta accepted the umbrella and thanked him with a smile.
b6.o0.refuerzo: That's it: the imperfecto paints the background of the story.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The indefinido tells completed events, not the background.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The future is not a past tense.
b6.pregunta: Which tense describes what the scene was like?
b7.frase: ____ en casa cuando sonó el teléfono.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: being at home is the background, and it goes in the imperfect.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Estuve» would close the stay; here it is only the scene.
b7.pregunta: You say where you were when the phone rang. What is missing?
b8.frase: Resulta que la había dejado en casa
b8.traduccion: It turns out I had left it at home
b9.frase: Me di cuenta de que ____ las llaves.
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Pierdo» is present; you talk about something earlier in the past.
b9.o1.refuerzo: Yes: losing them came before realising.
b9.pregunta: You lost the keys before realising. What is missing?
b10.o0.refuerzo: That's it: it expresses relief that everything ended well.
b10.o1.refuerzo: That expresses sadness, and the story ended well.
b10.o2.refuerzo: That is a strong denial, not a reaction of relief.
b10.pregunta: A friend ends a scary story happily. What do you say?
b12.o0.refuerzo: That expression opens the story; it does not move it on.
b12.o2.refuerzo: That's it: «luego» links one event with the next.
b12.pregunta: Which expression helps you move on to the next event?
p.pasó.consejo: Indefinido of «pasar» with «él»: the accent mark on the «ó» separates it from the present «pasa».
p.dejado.consejo: Participle of «dejar», regular. «La había dejado» means I had left it. The «j» sounds like «h».
p.siguiente.consejo: It has no feminine form: «la siguiente parada», «el día siguiente». The «gu» keeps the «g» hard.
p.volví.consejo: Indefinido of «volver» with «yo»: the accent mark on the «í». Both «v» sound like «b».
p.perdido.consejo: Participle of «perder», regular: «perd-» + «-ido». «Había perdido» means had lost.
p.encontré.consejo: Indefinido of «encontrar» with «yo»: regular, with an accent mark on the «é». The present is «encuentro».
p.bolsillo.consejo: It is masculine: «el bolsillo». It comes from «bolsa». The «ll» sounds like «y».
p.farolas.consejo: It is the plural of «la farola». In Latin America you also hear «el farol».
p.dibujaban.consejo: Imperfect of «dibujar» with «ellas»: «-aban» is the ending. It describes the scene.
p.círculos.consejo: It is the plural of «el círculo». The accent mark falls on the first syllable: «CÍR-cu-los».
p.amarillos.consejo: It is the masculine plural of «amarillo», agreeing with «círculos». The «ll» sounds like «y».
p.asfalto.consejo: It is masculine: «el asfalto». The «sf» keeps both sounds together.
p.mojado.consejo: It comes from «mojar». It changes with gender: «mojado», «mojada». The «j» sounds like «h».
p.volvía.consejo: Imperfect of «volver»: «volvía». It sets the background of the story. Both «v» sound like «b».
p.llenas.consejo: It is the feminine plural of «lleno», agreeing with «manos». It takes «de»: «llenas de bolsas».
p.bolsas.consejo: It is the plural of «la bolsa». In Spain «la bolsa» is also a plastic or paper bag.
p.olía.consejo: Imperfect of «oler»: «olía». It takes «a»: «olía a tierra mojada». Present: «huele».
p.castañas.consejo: It is the plural of «la castaña». The «ñ» sounds like «ny».
p.asadas.consejo: It comes from «asar». It agrees with «castañas»: feminine plural. Do not confuse «asar» with «azar».
p.olvidado.consejo: Participle of «olvidar», regular. «Había olvidado el paraguas» means she had left it behind by mistake.
p.velocidad.consejo: It ends in «-dad» and is feminine: «la velocidad». «A toda velocidad» means at full speed.
p.levantó.consejo: Indefinido of «levantar» with «él»: the accent mark on the «ó». Present: «levanta».
p.soltó.consejo: Indefinido of «soltar» with «ella». Present: «suelta», with «ue»; in the past it is regular.
p.gritó.consejo: Indefinido of «gritar» with «ella»: the accent mark on the «ó». Present: «grita».
p.desconocido.consejo: It is the masculine singular: «un desconocido». For a woman: «una desconocida».
p.escena.consejo: It is feminine: «la escena». The «sc» sounds «s-th»: «es-THE-na».
p.corrió.consejo: Indefinido of «correr» with «él»: the accent mark on the «ó». The «rr» is strong.
p.esperaron.consejo: Indefinido of «esperar» with «ellos»: regular ending «-aron». No accent mark.
p.aceptó.consejo: Indefinido of «aceptar» with «ella»: the accent mark on the «ó». Present: «acepta».
p.dio.consejo: Indefinido of «dar» with «él» or «ella». It has one syllable, so it has no accent mark. «Dar las gracias» is to thank.
p.imperfecto.consejo: It is masculine: «el imperfecto». It describes scenes: «era», «llovía», «estaba».
